source.title: When Truthful Representations Flip Under Deceptive Instructions?
source.authors: Xianxuan Long; Yao Fu; Runchao Li; Mu Sheng; Haotian Yu; Xiaotian Han; Pan Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some plotted SAE results have no numerical values in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Extends SAE feature analysis to two instruction-tuned LLMs and reports feature-level results on factual-verification datasets; it does not reproduce the original toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper measures SAE feature activations and their geometry under different prompts, including identifying specific responsive features. Linear-probe results and prompted output accuracy do not test the claim versions catalogued here; the cited toy-model superposition work is not a result of this study. The study does not test whether SAEs recover a complete or canonical feature set.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs (Llama Scope, Gemma Scope) as off-the-shelf tools to measure how deceptive instructions shift internal representations. The authors say they use SAEs 'purely as measurement tools.' No result bears on whether features are superposed, whether polysemanticity is capacity-driven, whether real models spread features across neurons, or whether SAE dictionaries are complete or canonical. The claim that PCA fails 'due to feature superposition' is asserted, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with three additions. The authors also conclude that the instructed True/False output is linearly decodable under all prompt types. They attribute PCA's failure on open-domain data to feature superposition, but assert this rather than test it. The location of the shifts is model-dependent: around layers 10–16 for Llama and mid-to-late layers (16–32) for Gemma.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies toy networks and superposition geometries; this paper analyzes frozen instruction-tuned LLMs with pretrained SAEs and compares factual-verification activations across prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported shifts vary by layer and dataset; the paper says shifts peak around Layer 16 for Llama and Layer 21 for Gemma, and notes that global PCA separates curated examples but not complex open-domain examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Deceptive instructions shift mean SAE feature vectors much more than neutral ones; truthful vs neutral stays near cos>0.95, overlap>0.80. A few top-ranked SAE features show near-binary activation by instruction type.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instructed deception produces layer-localized shifts in SAE feature space of instruction-tuned LLMs (a deception-representation claim, not superposition).

record.problems: SAE shift results are largely presented as plots without numerical values in the text. The analysis covers two models, English factual-verification data, and frozen weights; it does not causally intervene on the identified features. The paper acknowledges that SAE feature semantics are approximate and may depend on sparsity targets and training data.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the linear-probe accuracy or PCA results: these measure truth-label decodability/separation rather than a claim version. No truthful-versus-neutral SAE metric rows are included because they do not add evidence on the claim versions tested.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry of superposed features.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of the origins of polysemanticity.
There is no measure of features spread across neurons and no evaluation of SAE reconstruction or recovery. SAEs are applied as given.
No test of the completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features. The authors note feature semantics are approximate.
No comparison of one-dimensional versus multidimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. Using SAEs to find condition-sensitive features presupposes the SAE dictionary rather than testing feature recovery or neuron-level spreading. The study states it uses SAEs 'purely as measurement tools,' which places it in T4. The Llama analysis applies Base-model SAEs to the Instruct model.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature sparsity and importance effects, transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity pressure, competition between features, and dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study examines SAE features in two LLMs, but does not measure features spread across neurons or validate the completeness or recovery quality of the SAE dictionary.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features are not tested.
The study does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer-wise mean SAE feature vectors under deceptive and truthful prompts using cosine similarity.

conditions.value: shift described around 10–16; extremum at Layer 16

rows.measure: Cosine similarity of mean SAE feature vectors
rows.baseline: Truthful condition; numerical baseline figure only
rows.value: Figure only; text says cosine similarity plunges around layers 10–16
rows.note: The study reports a larger deceptive-versus-truthful feature shift than for neutral comparisons.
rows.check: This is a deceptive-vs-truthful shift in SAE feature space, a deception finding rather than a measure of superposition or SAE feature recovery. It is observed for the study's own question but bears on no version.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared activation of the second most deception-sensitive SAE feature under truthful and deceptive prompts.
rows.measure: SAE feature activation by prompt condition
rows.value: The feature is active almost exclusively under truthful prompts
rows.note: The text describes a clear separation in feature activation.
rows.check: The feature is selected post hoc as the largest truthful/deceptive activation difference, so its separation is partly a selection value. It shows condition sensitivity, not superposition or SAE recovery. The paper also states the Llama SAEs come from the Llama-3.1-8B-Base suite but are applied to the Instruct model.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-Instruct; tested factual-verification datasets and prompt conditions
reader_labels.reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs to identify sparse features and reports condition-dependent feature activations and geometry (r1–r14). This is indirect evidence of SAE features in these LLMs, not a test of dictionary completeness.
